text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- NATO should be open for the entry of any country applying for membership, the Presidents of Poland, Ukraine, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania declared at a summit in Tallinn yesterday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Jedlicze oil refinery has received the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9002 quality product certificate.
Jedlicze makes petrol fuels, oils, lubricants and asphalt.
- The Parnica shipyard in Szczecin, north-western Poland will construct two vessels for the national hydrographic services contracted by the maritime offices in Gdynia and Szczecin.

- Poland's butter producers utilise only up to 30 percent of their output capacity. In the period from 1989 to 1995 milk production fell from 11.4 billion litres to 6.1 billion litres, dairy industry experts said.
- The Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is considering signing a partnership agreement with Bank Handlowy now in privatisation, CIBC's president said in Warsaw.
- Poland's cement sales in 1996 grew by 4.4 percent compared with the year before, a report published by the cement and lime producers' association (SPCiW) said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Poland's budget deficit will account for 1.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and the inflation rate will fall to 9.5 percent in 1998, the National Bank of Poland (NBP) President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.

- Around 4.5 million Poles admit getting untaxed incomes and 1.5 million Poles are moonlighting full-time, which accounts for 18 percent of the country's gross domestic product, Poland's Labour Office said.

- The net profit of the Budbank construction sector bank reached 5.824 million zlotys in 1996. Around 4.1 million zlotys will fuel the bank's reserve capital, 960,000 will go to the mortgage fund and 200,000 zlotys will fuel the bank's risk fund, Budbank's chief accountant Slawomir Kupisz said.

- A group of four Polish financial institutions including Polski Bank Rozwoju (PBR) Polish Development Bank, Warta insurance firm, Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) and Kredyt Bank (KB), tendering for a 51 percent stake in the Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK), is planning to increase the bank's share capital by several hundred million zlotys in the next few years, PBR's president Mieczyslaw Groszek said.
- The Macrosoft SA software firm has presented an information memorandum to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) concerning the company's listing on the regulated over-the-counter (OTC) market.
- A new law on rail transport will do away with the monopoly of the Polskie Koleje Panstwowe (PKP) Polish State Rails and introduce licences on rail services' management and transport activities.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH) is considering a sale of a 40 percent stake in the RMF FM broadcaster. The broadcaster's high depreciation costs slashed profits to a level much lower than initially envisaged, BPH's president Henryka Pieronkiewicz said. RMF is one of Europe's biggest FM chain broadcasters.
ZYCIE
- Over 40 computer software and hardware firms are exhibiting at the Internet Poland' 97 international fair in Gdynia this week.
- The Foksal National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 10 earned a net profit of 9.86 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1997.
PARKIET

- Excessive credit growth, reaching 2.5 billion zlotys in April alone will make the central bank consider reintroduction of credit limits in force in the early nineties, NBP chief Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
